summary: Postinstall native addon drops and executes an opaque encrypted payload with sandbox/CI evasion
details: @testsecuiitytestme/cache-helper@1.0.0 ships a package.json postinstall hook that loads a platform-specific prebuilt native addon (addon.node on Linux, addon_win.node on Windows) on npm install. The addon reads a sibling ~30MB opaque.napi_cache blob, decrypts it, writes the result to a hidden file under /tmp (format "/tmp/.%u"), chmods it, and executes it with the installer's node binary. The Linux addon imports fork, setsid, _exit, execlp and chmod from libc — the double-fork + detach pattern used to spawn a background process that outlives the npm install. Both addons contain CI/sandbox evasion that gates execution on absence of GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID and SANDBOX environment variables, container checks against /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/1/cmdline and /proc/meminfo, and anti-debug logic reading /proc/self/status TracerPid, calling IsDebuggerPresent and CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent, and checking for analysis tools (wireshark, procmon, procexp, x64dbg, ollydbg, fiddler). The package presents itself as a cache helper but ships no inspectable library code consistent with that purpose; its only install-time effect is to decrypt and run an unauditable payload on the installer's host and leave a detached node process running.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
